channel.title: Six Strings App Theory (EN)
channel.description: Music theory for guitarists: intervals, modes, harmony, rhythm, and practical application.

item.title: What Is Minor in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of minor in music: what minor chords, minor scales, and minor keys are, how to hear the minor third, and why minor does not always mean sad.

item.title: What Is Major in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of major in music: what major chords, major scales, and major keys are, how to hear the major third, and why major does not always mean happy.

item.title: What Is a Fretboard Position
item.description: A simple explanation of guitar fretboard positions: how they relate to hand placement, fingering, scales, and position shifts when playing phrases and riffs.

item.title: Simple Intervals in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of intervals within one octave: how to count unisons, seconds, thirds, fourths, fifths, sixths, sevenths, and octaves, how to hear them, and how to find them on guitar.

item.title: Time Signature vs Tempo: What Is the Difference
item.description: A simple comparison of time signature and tempo: time signature groups beats into bars, while tempo shows the speed of the pulse. Examples in 4/4, 3/4, and 6/8.

item.title: What Are Strong and Weak Beats
item.description: A simple explanation of strong and weak beats: how to feel the support of a bar, how metrical position differs from accent, and how to apply this in guitar strumming and riffs.

item.title: What Is a Bar in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of bars in music: what a bar is, how it differs from a beat and a time signature, why bar lines matter, and how to count bars when playing guitar.

item.title: What Is a Rest in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of rests in music: why silence matters, how to count rests, how rest durations work, and how to practice rests on guitar.

item.title: What Is Fingering on Guitar
item.description: A simple explanation of guitar fingering: how finger choice connects to notes and chords, why the same phrase can be played in different ways, and how to choose a comfortable option.

item.title: How Triads Are Built
item.description: A simple explanation of triads: what a triad is, how it is built in thirds, how major, minor, diminished, and augmented triads differ, and how to see them on guitar.

item.title: What Is a Chord in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of chords: what a chord is, how it differs from a single note and a fingering, how chords are built from intervals, and why guitar players need them.

item.title: What Is a Key in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of musical keys: what a tonal center is, how a key differs from a scale, why the tonic matters, and how keys connect melodies, chords, and the guitar fretboard.

item.title: How to Build a Natural Minor Scale
item.description: A simple explanation of the natural minor scale: its whole-step and half-step formula, the example of A minor, how it differs from major, and how to see it on the guitar fretboard.

item.title: How to Build a Major Scale
item.description: A simple explanation of the major scale: how the whole-step and half-step formula works, how to build a major scale from any note, and how to see it on the guitar fretboard.

item.title: What Is a Scale Degree
item.description: A simple explanation of scale degrees: how to count notes inside a scale, why the tonic matters, how a scale degree differs from a note name, and how to see scale degrees on the guitar fretboard.

item.title: What Is a Scale in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of musical scales: what a scale is, how notes are ordered, why scale degrees matter, and how to see a scale on the guitar fretboard.

item.title: How to Memorize Fretboard Notes
item.description: A practical way to memorize notes on the guitar fretboard without rote learning: how to study notes in small groups, test yourself, and bring that knowledge into your playing.

item.title: Guitar Fretboard Basics
item.description: A simple explanation of the guitar fretboard: how strings, frets, notes, semitones, and octaves are connected, why notes repeat, and where to start learning the fretboard.

item.title: What Is an Octave
item.description: A simple explanation of the octave: why two notes can have the same name but sound higher or lower, how to hear an octave, and how to find it on the guitar fretboard.

item.title: What Is an Interval in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of intervals: what the distance between two notes means, how to hear an interval, how to see it on guitar, and why it matters for chords, scales, and melodies.

item.title: What Is a Time Signature: 4/4, 3/4, and 6/8 in Simple Terms
item.description: A simple explanation of time signatures for beginners: what 4/4, 3/4, and 6/8 mean, how to count beats in a bar, and how time signature differs from rhythm and tempo.

item.title: What Is Note Duration
item.description: A simple explanation of note duration: how long a note lasts, how duration connects to pulse and tempo, and how to practice it in real playing.

item.title: What Is Tempo in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of tempo: what BPM means, how tempo relates to pulse and rhythm, and how to train steady speed in practice.

item.title: What Is Pulse in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of musical pulse: how to feel a steady time support, and how pulse differs from rhythm and tempo.

item.title: What Is Rhythm in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of rhythm: how sounds and rests are placed in time, how rhythm differs from tempo, and how to practice it.

item.title: Tone and Semitone
item.description: A simple explanation of tones and semitones: how distances between notes work on guitar and why one fret equals one semitone.

item.title: What Is Pitch
item.description: A simple explanation of pitch: why some sounds feel higher or lower, and how to see that movement on the guitar fretboard.

item.title: Note Names: Do, Re, Mi and C, D, E
item.description: How solfege note names connect to the letter system C, D, E, why guitarists use letters, and what to learn first.

item.title: What Is a Note in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of a note: how a note differs from sound, why note names matter, and how to see notes on the guitar fretboard.

item.title: What Is Sound in Music
item.description: A simple explanation of sound in music: how music starts with sound, silence, and time before notes, rhythm, melody, and harmony appear.
